Ten scouts under Asim bin Thabit are surrounded by Bani Lihyan; Asim and six fall, Khubaib, sold in Mecca, prays two rak'at before being killed, and wasps guard Asim's body.
Free captives, feed the hungry, visit the sick; Ali's paper lists freeing captives; Al-Abbas's ransom is not waived; and a Badr captive hears the Prophet recite Surat at-Tur at Maghrib.
An infidel spy sits with the companions on a journey and leaves; at the Prophet's order Salama chases and kills him and is given the spy's belongings.
Stabbed, Umar urges his successor to keep the covenant with non-Muslims under Allah's and His Apostle's protection, fight to defend them and not tax them beyond their means.
Weeping, Ibn Abbas recalls the Thursday the Prophet's illness worsened: people disputed his call for writing materials, and he ordered the pagans expelled from Arabia and delegates honoured.
Umar urges buying a silk cloak for Eid and delegations; the Prophet says it is worn by one with no share in the Hereafter, yet sends Umar one to sell.
The Prophet tests young Ibn Saiyad and stops Umar killing him; later he warns that the Dajjal, of whom every prophet warned, is one-eyed, and Allah is not.
Asked on his Hajj where he will stay, the Prophet asks whether Aqil left them any house and names Khaif Bani Kinana, where Quraish swore to boycott Bani Hashim.
Umar tells his Hima manager not to oppress, to admit small herds but not those of the rich, and reserves the people's land only for mounts used in Allah's Cause.
Listing those who had professed Islam at the Prophet's order, the companions count 1,500 and wonder whether they need fear, yet later trials force some to pray alone in fear.
A man enlisted for a campaign whose wife is leaving for Hajj is told by the Prophet to go back and perform Hajj with her.
The Prophet calls a man claiming Islam one of the Fire; he fights fiercely, then kills himself when wounded, and the Prophet announces that only a Muslim enters Paradise.
Weeping, the Prophet announces Zaid, Ja'far and Abdullah bin Rawaha martyred before Khalid took the flag unappointed and was given victory; seventy Ansar are betrayed and killed at Bi'r Ma'una.
After conquering a people the Prophet stayed three days in their town, and he set out for Umrah from Al-Ji'rana, where he shared out the Hunain booty.
Ibn Umar's horse and runaway slave, lost to the enemy and the Byzantines, are returned to him once the Muslims win, Khalid bin Al-Walid restoring them.
Jabir invites the Prophet and a few others to a young sheep and a Sa of barley, but the Prophet loudly calls the people of the Trench to come.
The Prophet praises Um Khalid's yellow shirt in Ethiopian, lets her play with the seal of prophethood, and three times wishes her to wear it out, and she lived long.
When Al-Hasan bin Ali puts a charity date in his mouth, the Prophet stops him in Persian, saying they do not eat charity.
The Prophet calls Ghulul a great sin whose doers bear animals, gold or clothes on their necks at Resurrection, beyond his intercession; Karkara, who stole booty, is in the Fire.
Pots cooked before the booty's division are overturned; ten sheep count as a camel; a runaway camel may be shot; and any blood-letting tool but tooth or nail may slaughter.
Jarir, for whom the Prophet prayed to sit firm, leads 150 Ahmas riders to dismantle and burn Dhul-Khalasa, the Yemeni Ka'bah, and the Prophet blesses them five times.
No migration remains after the Conquest of Mecca, only jihad and good intention; the Prophet takes Mujalid's pledge for Islam instead, and Aisha says the same.
Ali recounts seizing Hatib's letter and the Prophet excusing him as a Badr warrior, words a supporter of Uthman says emboldened Ali to shed blood.
Boys meet the returning Prophet, who says 'we return repentant', is aided by Abu Talha when his camel slips with Safiya, and prays two rak'at in the mosque.
Ali's two she-camels, from his Badr booty and the Khumus, are mutilated by Hamza drinking with Ansari men; the Prophet rebukes him, but seeing him drunk, withdraws.
Abu Bakr refuses Fatima her inheritance from the Prophet's Fai, as prophets leave only charity; Umar, judging Ali and Abbas, explains how the Prophet and his successors managed that property.
The Abdul Qais delegation are told to believe in Allah, pray, pay zakat, fast Ramadan and pay a fifth of booty, and are forbidden four vessels used for alcoholic drinks.
The Prophet's heirs take no Dinar, all beyond his wives' and workers' expenses being charity; he left some barley in Aisha's house, his arms, a white mule and charity land.
In his last illness the Prophet is nursed in Aisha's house with his wives' leave, and dies there leaning on her chest after she softens a siwak for him.
Walking Safiya back from his I'tikaf, the Prophet tells two passing Ansari men she is his wife, as Satan circulates in people like blood and might plant suspicion.
Ibn Umar saw the Prophet in Hafsa's house relieving himself with his back to the Qibla, facing Sham.
The Prophet prayed Asr while the sun still shone in Aisha's dwelling.
In a sermon the Prophet points toward Aisha's house, eastward, saying three times that affliction will come from there, where the side of Satan's head appears.
Hearing a man ask to enter Hafsa's house, the Prophet says he is her foster uncle, as whatever blood relations forbid, foster relations forbid too.
The Prophet's ring, engraved Muhammad Apostle Allah, seals Abu Bakr's letter; Anas shows his worn shoes, Aisha the patched garment he died in, and his cup is mended with silver.
Al-Miswar, offering to guard the Prophet's sword, recalls his sermon when Ali sought Abu Jahl's daughter: Fatima is from him, and the two cannot be one man's wives.
Ali sends his son with a document of the Prophet's rules on charity to Uthman for his Zakat officials, and Uthman declines it.
Instead of a servant from booty slave girls, the Prophet teaches Fatima and Ali bedtime words: Allahu Akbar 34 times, Al-hamdu lillah and Subhan Allah 33 each.
People may name sons after the Prophet but not use his kunya, for he is Qasim, the distributor; he praises the Ansar for refusing that title to a boy's father.
Allah gives religious understanding to whom He wills good; He is the Giver and the Prophet only the distributor, giving as ordered, and this nation stays victorious.
